about: What a model of [JEngine] will structurally be unable to predict, one record each: claim, mechanism, evidence, asserted_value, source. See felizjueves.literature.limits.

limits.claim: exact_given_inputs on jengine/table1 (FLOPs): no recovered set of inputs reproduces all 40 printed cells. The cut IS recovered (plan/recovery.py, two-ended nearest fill per direction, which also gives all 40 of Table 3); the sieve's inputs are not. Refused under the rules-only doctrine (#108): a per-cell fitted seed order is not admitted as a recovered input.
limits.mechanism: Table 1 is post-sieve, and the sieve's output depends on its seed order: an order of a batch's targets, up to 969! of them at L = 16, one batch. [JEngine, v2, §4.1] says the order moves FLOPs and node count by up to ~2%, and that the authors did not optimise it; they do not state the order they used. So the order is an unpublished input with no rule to recover it from, and the printed cells sit inside its spread. Also unpublished, and searched below: which other direction a re-parented child takes, how far the upward sweep deletes, and whether the walk is breadth- or depth-first.
limits.evidence: Every search below uses the recovered cut and the counting conventions #10 fixed (1/2/3 FLOPs per node by r_d; fundamentals with m > 0 are intermediates). (1) The literal sieve seeded in hermite_targets order: 9/40 exact, (7,3) (7,6) (7,9) (8,6) (8,9) (9,6) (9,9) (10,9) (11,9). (2) The literal sieve over plan/recovery.py's 26 structured seed orders (hermite_targets and its reverse; |r| ascending or descending, then the components in each of the 6 axis orders, all ascending or all descending): best 17/40 ('|r| asc, then xzy desc'). (3) A scratch variant of the sieve, not kept in the repo, over those 26 orders x 7 re-expansion choices (smallest r_d', largest r_d', xyz, zyx, smallest r_d' ties to z, cyclic successor, cyclic predecessor) x 2 sweeps (every orphaned node, or only i and its parents upward) x breadth- or depth-first x [r-1d] or [r-2d] enqueued first: 1456 configurations, best 17/40 Table 1 together with 29/40 Table 2. (4) Random seed orders, each sieved twice (smallest- and largest-r_d' re-expansion): 6000 runs (3000 orders) at (7,1) and at (8,1) reach the printed pair in 3578 and 460 of them, so those cells ARE seed-order effects; 600 runs (300 orders) at (16,1) never reach it (best FLOPs 5666 against the printed 5633; the hermite order gives 5644), so the paper's order there is in the tail, and no rule this search knows names it. Bounded at that point on purpose: the remaining space is the factorial order space itself, and searching it for each cell would be a per-cell fit. (5) #108, THE WIDENED FAMILY: plan/recovery.py's seed_orders(widened=True), the 26 above plus 32 rules each with a stated rationale (FLOPs of the target's MILD closure asc/desc; out-degree of its MILD parents asc/desc; sieve-greedy, by how many of its parents already pass Alg. 3's test, desc/asc; direction-major by batch_direction in the 6 axis orders; max-then-mid component in the 4 sign combinations, '+max/-mid' being the predecessor tree's base rule), each with hermite and reversed-hermite tie-breaks: 58 orders, literal sieve, recovered cut. Table 3 stays 40/40 under every one. Best Table 1: 33/40, one order only, '+max/-mid, ties reversed' (max component ascending, middle descending, then reversed hermite position); the same order is the unique best on Table 2 (38/40). Its 7 Table 1 misses are (13,3) (14,3) (15,1) (15,3) (16,1) (16,3) (16,6), every one OVER the printed FLOPs (+0.11% to +0.32%), and its 2 Table 2 misses (15,3) (16,1) are both UNDER the printed intermediates: the residual has one sign per table, the same trade test_plan_sieve.py's anchors show for the hermite order, which points at a choice inside the sieve (re-expansion), not at the seed order. That order was picked by its score from 58 named rules, so 33 is itself a selection over rules; it is still a rule applied to every cell, and it does not reach 40. THE DECISION (#108): RULES ONLY. exact_given_inputs records rules the paper's numbers were produced by, the same for every cell; a per-cell fitted order is not admitted, not even under a separately named rule. Reasons: (a) the predecessor tree's per-cell orders show a fit exists (all 40 cells of Tables 1-3, 29 cells needing no transposition, the rest 1-5 swaps off its own '+max/-mid' rule, found by a beam search scored against the Article's numbers), but those values do not transfer (a different cut recovery and seed-order family), and a fit shows only that some order reproduces a number, which is evidence of nothing about the method; (b) the one-sign residual above says a fit here would absorb a systematic difference in the sieve into per-cell inputs, so the fitted record would be wrong about what it records. The 7 cells stand at their printed values.

asserted_value.printed_values_stand: the 31 cells above, under the recovered cut and the literal sieve seeded in hermite_targets order; their printed values are taken from the table as published

limits.claim: at_or_under on the searched board, jengine/table1 (FLOPs) and jengine/table2 (max intermediates): 21 cells of Table 1 and 3 of Table 2 stay over the printed value under the searched plans. Table 3 is at or under in all 40. Every residual cell is over by at most +2.04%, and all but one by at most +1.04%.
limits.mechanism: The printed cells are post-sieve, and the sieve's output depends on its seed order, which [JEngine, v2, §4.1] says moves FLOPs and node count by up to ~2%, was not optimised, and is not stated (the jengine/table1 exact_given_inputs record above has the full argument). The residual margins sit inside that spread: the paper's numbers are one draw from the seed-order space, and in these cells the draw is better than any order in the bounded family searched. Reaching it means searching the factorial order space per cell, which is a per-cell fit to the printed answer, not a generator choice. The one margin at the edge of the spread, (16, 1) Table 1 at +2.04%, is the objective's price: putting intermediates before FLOPs takes a seed order with 2 fewer intermediates and 104 more FLOPs; the literal hermite order is +0.20% there and the cell is over either way.
limits.evidence: plan/search.py, exhaustive per (L, n_batches) and recorded in data/scoreboards/jengine/searched_cuts.json. SEARCHED: every shared contiguous cut (C(L, k - 1), at most 120 per cell) crossed with plan/recovery.py's 26 structured seed orders, at most 3120 full plans per cell (partition, MILD DAG per batch, sieve, PlanCost). OBJECTIVE, stated before scoring and not tuned to it: feasible if max targets <= the cell's minimax + 1 (the minimax tolerance), then fewest max intermediates, then fewest FLOPs; ties to the lowest cut, then seed_orders() order. RESULT: Table 1 21/40 over, Table 2 3/40, Table 3 0/40 (the first search, cut only and minimax tolerance 0, had 30, 13, 0 and a worst margin of +7.50% at (15, 9) Table 2; the tolerance closes that cell in all three tables). UNREACHABLE, independent of the objective: in every residual cell, NO candidate in the whole searched space -- any cut, any of the 26 orders, any number of targets -- is at or under the printed value in all three tables at once; in each the smallest FLOPs any feasible candidate reaches is still over Table 1. NOT SEARCHED: per-direction cuts, seed orders outside the structured family, the sieve's re-expansion choice and sweep (the jengine/table1 record above searched those against exact_given_inputs and stopped at 17/40), and no-sieve.

asserted_value.printed_values_stand: the cells above, with their margin in percent over the printed value; their printed values are taken from the tables as published

limits.claim: [JEngine, v2, §4.1]'s comparison of MILD against Johnson et al.'s near-optimal tree search (the paper's refs 59/60): MILD 1-2% behind on FLOPs and 2-6% ahead on intermediates. Not reproducible on this machine; this repo's own measurement replaces it rather than reproducing it.
limits.mechanism: The search the paper compares against is not here: neither its code nor its output is available, and the paper does not state the grid, the cost convention or the reference point on a frontier that its percentages were taken against. A number computed here therefore measures a different comparison -- this tree's optimum (plan/optimum.py, exact over one reduction direction per materialised node with nodes shared; no algebraic rewriting, no recompute) under this tree's cost model (plan/cost.py) -- and cannot confirm or refute the printed one, only stand in its place.
limits.evidence: data/literature/jengine/mild_vs_optimum.json, recomputed by test/test_mild_vs_optimum.py (#111). Exact range L = 0..5: MILD equals the optimum for L <= 4 and at L = 5 is (51, 161) against (48, 160), behind on both axes, +6.25% intermediates and +0.625% FLOPs -- not the paper's shape (behind on FLOPs, ahead on intermediates). Every exact frontier there is a single point, so no scheme in the space is ahead of it on either axis. On the published grid a width-16 beam proves MILD at least 0.743% and 0.73% behind on FLOPs at L = 11 and 12 (dominated on both axes) and proves nothing elsewhere.

asserted_value.printed_values_stand: the paper's percentages are taken as published; this repo's gap is recorded beside them, not reconciled with them. No scoreboard, no rule: board and rule are null.

limits.claim: jengine/batching-crosses-our-ridge, #114's own claim: does batching move OUR [p|q] kernels across OUR cards' ridge? Answered on sm_86 only. gfx1200's answer is ABSENT (could not measure), and no answer here says anything about [JEngine, v2, Fig. 7]'s A100 result, which stands as the paper's and is not ours to dispute.
limits.mechanism: (1) THE RIDGE IS THE CARD'S. A verdict is intensity against peak fp64 over bandwidth, and our measured ridges -- 0.65 FLOP/B on sm_86 and 1.49 on gfx1200, ACHIEVABLE rates from this box's probes (data/measured/ceilings.json, #109), not datasheet peaks -- are each that card's; Fig. 7's A100 ridge is a different number, from a different card, and no comparison is drawn with it. Consumer fp64 is cut hard on both of our cards, so a class may be compute-bound ALREADY AT ONE BATCH here, and on sm_86 three of the four subgrid L are: that is a statement about the card, not about batching, and not a contradiction of the paper. (2) THE AMD ANSWER IS ABSENT. gfx1200 has no counter rows (measured_store.UNMEASURED, #112), and since #140 the refusal is FINAL: rocprofv3 1.1.0 now loads in this container, but rocprofiler-sdk defines no fp64 instruction counter for gfx12 (SQ_INSTS_VALU_*_F64 exist for CDNA only), so it gives no measured FLOP count and hence no measured intensity; and its GL2C byte counters read 0 on this box, so it gives no bytes either. Could not measure is recorded as such, never as 'never crossed'. (3) WHAT THE INTENSITY SEES. The bytes are ncu's DRAM traffic (32-byte sectors) on ONE input, #53's wide-T (2048 x 128), in a counter run that serialises and replays each kernel; a batch whose working set stays in L2 hardly touches DRAM, so a split cell's kernel intensities spread over orders of magnitude, and another input or cache could move a verdict near the ridge. The verdict is a threshold, not a margin: L = 13 at 1 batch is compute-bound at 0.96 FLOP/B against 0.65. (4) WHICH CLASSES. SUBGRID's L are 7, 10, 13 and 16, with b in {1, 3, 6, 9, 12}: L = 10 is Fig. 7's [5|5], L = 13 and 16 bracket its [7|7], and [6|6] (L = 12) is not measured (#112 measured the compile cost and declined it). (5) THE PER-KERNEL VARIANT AT ONE BATCH IS THE CELL: a one-batch partition is one kernel, so the two variants can differ only past 1 batch; on sm_86 they do not differ at all. (6) WHAT THE FLOPS COUNT (#116). The numerator is every fp64 instruction the kernel issues (ncu's dadd + dmul + 2 dfma), the Boys evaluation included, whereas [JEngine, v2, Table 1]'s FLOPs exclude the Boys function; an intensity here is not Table 1's FLOPs over any byte count, and the counter run, which serialises and replays each kernel, is not the timed run (counter_ns is never a timing). (7) THE CEILINGS ARE ACHIEVABLE RATES, at the clock the card ran them (#141): the ridges come from this box's probes, not datasheets. The #116 assumption -- that gfx1200's published fp64 figure (0.801 TFLOPS) could count RDNA4's fp32 dual-issue -- is RETIRED, not assumed: a GRBM_GUI_ACTIVE cycle count puts the probe at 127.95 flop per GPU cycle, the single-issue 2 fp64 FMA lanes per CU per clock (32 CUs x 2 x 2 = 128; the probe is plain v_fma_f64, and VOPD dual-issue has no f64 form), so its sanity bound is now per clock (published.gfx1200.per_clock). The recorded 0.446 TFLOPS is ~111% of the 0.4006 TFLOPS rated-boost figure because the card ran the probe at a counted ~3.49 GHz, above its 3130 MHz rated boost: the 1.49 FLOP/B ridge is the card at that clock, and a clock-limited run of the same card would have a lower one. gfx1200 has no verdict to move.
limits.evidence: felizjueves.ridge over data/measured/roofline.json (124 kernel rows, 20 cells, sm_86, ncu 2025.3.1.0, recorded by #112 behind the card gate), recomputed by test/test_ridge.py::test_batching_crosses_our_ridge_on_sm_86_and_gfx1200_could_not_measure. sm_86, both variants identical: L = 7, 10, 13 compute-bound already at 1 batch (300, 3.54, 0.96 FLOP/B), compute-bound at every higher count too; L = 16 memory-bound at 1 batch (0.40 FLOP/B) and crossed at 3 (cell 1.52 FLOP/B, smallest kernel 1.46), compute-bound at 6, 9, 12 as well. gfx1200: could not measure. CROSS-READ AGAINST #60 (9 batches do not suffice on either card): on sm_86 every kernel of every 9-batch cell is compute-bound, so the roofline does NOT explain #60's verdict as kernels still memory-bound at 9 -- it contradicts that reading. sm_86's 9 fails #60 only on SPILL (12 spills less at L = 13 and 16) while 12 is slower than 9 at every L on both inputs; the roofline agrees with the clock there, since there is no ridge left to cross at 9. On gfx1200, where 12 wins on near-T at L = 16, the roofline can say nothing: no rows.

limits.claim: jengine/ket-sort-key-beats-the-global-max on our cards (#147): the per-record product key I_q * max_q |D_q| against one global max|D|, same tau, molecule and batch count, both arms in one gated session per card. The declared expectation -- the global key is worse -- is CONTRADICTED on sm_86 and on gfx1200; two of the eight cells are below what this box can resolve.
limits.mechanism: (1) THE SCREEN. I_pair (ao/pairs.py) is pair-factor-free: a ket's Gaussian pair factor and dressing live in its dressed D_q, so its distance decay reaches the screen only through Dmax. A global Dmax erases it, and on every input here the global key skips NO (bra, ket) record pair, at either tau -- the screen's work goes the expected way, by the whole of the product's skips. (2) THE ORDER. The global key changes the ket order too (by I_q alone, i.e. by exponent and pair momentum) and that order is not free: on the two-H2 chain at tau = 1e-10 the product arm skips 560 of 8100 pairs and is still slower than the global arm, which skips none, by 21% on sm_86 and 9% on gfx1200 -- the two arms differ in ket order and keys only. At tau = 1e-3 (2790 skipped) the skips win. Why the product order costs time is NOT measured here; a candidate is the per-ket work of the device Boys (emit/_c.py's Kummer loop, whose length grows with T), grouped by exponent under the I_q order and interleaved under the product order, so lanes diverge more. (3) THE NOISE FLOOR is #60's: the larger of the two arms' IQRs over 31 timed builds. On sm_86 the H2O/cc-pVDZ builds are bimodal (near 8.5 and near 10 ms, IQRs 1.3-1.6 ms), so its two cc-pVDZ cells are the weakest: tau = 1e-3 reads BETTER by 1.57 ms over a 1.36 ms floor, tau = 1e-10 UNRESOLVED. On gfx1200 the cc-pVDZ tau = 1e-3 arms are equal to 3 us (UNRESOLVED) while tau = 1e-10 reads BETTER by 1.69 ms over a 0.25 ms floor. The chain cells resolve on both cards (IQRs under 13 us). (4) THE INPUTS: the chain is two H2, not #88's four, because the four-H2 sweep asks the card's fj_boys for T up to 1289, past its witnessed [0, 500] and its overflow near 700; the four-H2 chain's skip counts (66060 and 36072 of 104976 for the product, 0 for the global key) are the oracle's only.
limits.evidence: data/measured/builds.json, arm 'sort-ab', host e614efd48a48 (container), RTX 3080 (nvcc 13.0) and RX 9060 XT (hipcc / ROCm 7.2.4), one session per card, no phase discarded by the gate; verdicts computed by measured_store.sort_key_ab and pinned by test/test_measured.py::test_the_sort_key_verdict_is_contradicted_on_both_cards; skip counts recomputed by the launch oracle in test/test_launch_oracle.py::test_both_sort_keys_hold_the_screens_bound, which also holds both keys' J within tau * scale of J(0). Medians, product against global: sm_86 cc-pVDZ 1e-3 10080.9 / 8510.4 us (BETTER), 1e-10 10451.9 / 9836.6 us (UNRESOLVED), chain 1e-3 255.4 / 285.7 us (WORSE), 1e-10 346.7 / 285.7 us (BETTER); gfx1200 cc-pVDZ 1e-3 7066.6 / 7063.6 us (UNRESOLVED), 1e-10 8750.3 / 7059.9 us (BETTER), chain 1e-3 211.6 / 251.5 us (WORSE), 1e-10 273.8 / 251.0 us (BETTER).

asserted_value.expected: the global key is worse (#147, declared before the rows)
asserted_value.printed_values_stand: [JEngine, v2, §3.3]'s choice of key is taken as published for its kernel on its A100; this record is about our kernel on our cards. No scoreboard, no rule: board and rule are null.

limits.claim: A `Launch` IR and a `LaunchCost` model for the whole-molecule J of [JEngine, v2, §6]: DELIBERATELY ABSENT (#148, milestone 6's description (c), decided before any of its code). No IR represents the launch sequence, no model predicts what a whole build costs, and so nothing here ranks one launch plan above another or says the plan's order is the BEST one. J resident on the card across SCF iterations is out of scope by the same decision.
limits.mechanism: Milestone 6 makes the plan a VALUE and nothing else: `launch.LaunchPlan` (#138) says which [p|q] kernels run, over which index records, in which order. Each consumer checks the plan directly instead of going through a fourth representation of it: the launch oracle `launch.walk` (#142, pure Python, equal to the host's screened sweep to 0), the staged interpreted driver `ao/staged.py` (#143), and the device `main()` that `test/plan_driver.py` writes from a plan for the card (#144). That driver lives under `test/`, not `src/felizjueves/emit/`: the generator still emits kernels, not launch code. A `LaunchCost` would model a build with only the clock to score it against. The one per-kernel model this repo has, `lower.KernelCost`, already mis-ranks the measured rows it is scored against (data/measured/limits.json, #54 and #60). So the build is MEASURED (data/measured/builds.json, #146) and never predicted. The only ordering question put to the clock is #147's single A/B of two sort keys, and its declared expectation was contradicted on both cards (the jengine/ket-sort-key-beats-the-global-max record above). Residency stops at one build. Every timed build zeroes its J_p buffers, launches, and reads them back. The uploads happen once per process, outside the clock. Eq. 20's back-transform and the J_ab scatter run host-side in Python. Moving those to the device is milestone 7's subject.
limits.evidence: test/test_layering.py: the `launch` rule bans `emit`, `interp`, `measured`, `measured_store` and `literature`, and its transitive test holds `launch` off `reference/`, `interp`, `emit`, `ao.drive`, `ao.staged`, `dispatch`, `measured` and `measured_store` through any chain of imports. Nothing under src/ is named or defines a Launch IR or a LaunchCost; `interp.Launch` is the thread geometry, which is why the plan's unit is `ClassLaunch` (milestone (a)). The `timed_region` in data/measured/builds.json's header (`measured_store.BUILD_TIMED_REGION`) puts the H2D uploads, the host staging, eq. 20 and the scatter outside the clock.

asserted_value.printed_values_stand: Nothing in [JEngine, v2, §6] is scored against this; the record says what this repo chose not to build. No scoreboard, no rule: board and rule are null.

limits.claim: The screen's granularity, compared with the predecessor `jgen`: `jgen` maps one warp per SHELL PAIR and screens per shell pair, while this repo maps one warp per PRIMITIVE-PAIR RECORD and screens per record (#138, milestone 6's description (b)). This is a READING of [JEngine, v2, Alg. 1], not a defect on either side. Every n_pairs, n_skipped, skip fraction and launch-list length this repo records counts record pairs. None of them is comparable one for one with a shell-pair screen's count.
limits.mechanism: Alg. 1 reads a per-index Ip / Iq and does not say what an index is. This repo's bound, `I_pair` (ao/pairs.py), is pair-factor-free and proved per primitive-pair record (test/test_ao_pairs.py, over randomised geometry). The kernel contract maps one warp per bra record, by index. So the launch lists are record lists grouped by class. The plan carries the record -> shell pair map (`PairRec.shell_pair`, and its bra-side inverse `ClassLaunch.bra_blocks`) because eq. 20 accumulates into J_mn per shell pair. Both readings are Alg. 1. This one is finer, and it is the one with a proof here. How `jgen`'s shell-pair bound relates to `I_pair` was NOT measured, and no skip count here is set against `jgen`'s.
limits.evidence: src/felizjueves/launch.py's docstring, RECORDS, NOT SHELL PAIRS; test/test_launch.py, where every record of every shell pair the unique sweep visits appears exactly once and the record -> shell pair map round-trips; the launch oracle equal to `ao.j.coulomb_matrix_screened` to 0, with equal n_pairs and n_skipped, on the same records (test/test_launch_oracle.py). At this granularity H2O/cc-pVDZ has 351649 (bra, ket) record pairs (data/measured/builds.json, build:n_pairs).

asserted_value.printed_values_stand: Alg. 1 is taken as published; the record says which reading of its index this repo implements. No scoreboard, no rule: board and rule are null.

limits.claim: The whole-molecule J built from the launch plan on the card (#144, #146, #147), and what it does not reach. (1) THE DEVICE BOYS: the card's `fj_boys` is witnessed on T in [0, 500] only and overflows near T = 700, well below `reference.boys`' T_MAX = 2000, so the host ladder's four-H2 chain (T up to 1289) has no on-card build. (2) THE CLASSES: the tracked J fixtures stop at d (H2O/cc-pVDZ, pair momenta up to 4, classes L <= 8), so no on-card build reaches a class whose measured dispatch choice is above 1. (3) WHAT THE PLAN SAVED: the per-pair launch path (`ao.drive.KernelJP`-shaped) was not timed in #146's session, so no row says what building from the plan saves against it. (4) gfx1200's one-off upload is not explained.
limits.mechanism: (1) `fj_boys` (emit/_c.py's BOYS_DEVICE) is the Kummer series, exp(-T) times a sum of positive terms that grows like e^T. The sum overflows double near T = 709, before the exp(-T) factor can bring it back. `reference.boys` switched to a measured asymptote from T = 125 (#122), and the device routine did not. (2) Dispatch (#145) has rows only for the SUBGRID's L in {7, 10, 13, 16}, each for that L's own split (ceil(L/2), floor(L/2)); every other class falls back to 1. On the wide-T input the measured choice is 1 at every L on both cards. On near-T it is above 1 from L = 10 on gfx1200 and from L = 13 on sm_86, and those splits need pair momenta of 5 and 7, past cc-pVDZ's 4. The one dispatched cell on the card, H2O/cc-pVDZ with the wide-T resolver, therefore runs every class at 1: 24 by fallback and (4, 3) from its measured row. (3) #146 left the optional same-session reference out. (4) The uploads happen once per process, outside the timed region, recorded only as raw build:upload_ns, a single observation.
limits.evidence: (1) test/test_kernel_device.py checks `fj_boys` on [0, 500]; measured_store's docstring, THE SORT KEY, says why #147's chain is two H2 (T up to 188; three reach 615, four reach 1289). The four-H2 chain's skip counts come from the launch oracle alone (test/test_launch_oracle.py). (2) test/test_j_launched_ondevice.py's dispatched cell asserts every class at `dispatch.choose`'s count, and that (4, 3) is the measured one. (3) PR #183. (4) data/measured/builds.json: gfx1200's build:upload_ns is 21.9 to 35.8 ms across its 11 rows, against 0.10 to 0.16 ms across sm_86's 11.

asserted_value.printed_values_stand: [JEngine, v2, Alg. 1]'s per-molecule build is taken as published for its kernel on its A100; this record says how far this repo's on-card build reaches. No scoreboard, no rule: board and rule are null.
